WATCH: Japanese Embassy Infrastructure Attaché Akito Kinoshita presents the Pasig-Marikina River Channel Improvement Project (PMRCIP) and its importance in easing the effects of flooding in Metro Manila at the Rosario J.S. Water Leveling Station in Pasig City on Wednesday (March 25, 2026).

In particular, Akito said the PMRCIP was projected to have reduced the effects of Typhoon Ulysses in 2020 in Metro Manila from USD1.3 billion to USD0.3 billion in damages in addition to reducing the number of affected persons from an estimated 1 million people to 0.03 million people.

The PMRCIP is only one of the flood control projects supported by the Japanese government through the Official Development Assistance for the Philippines. | Raymond Carl Dela Cruz

#IntegratedStateMedia
#ISM
#PhilippineNewsAgency

Message to U.S. Citizens: Demonstration Alert: Nationwide Transportation Strike – March 26-27, 2026
https://t.co/EJ7RSI8Vwm

The U.S. Embassy informs U.S. citizens that a two-day nationwide transportation strike is scheduled for Thursday, March 26 through Friday, March 27, 2026.  Transport groups – including jeepney, bus, UV Express, and transport network vehicle service (TNVS) drivers – have said they plan to strike to demand government action on rising fuel prices.
The U.S. Embassy remains open and will continue to provide all public services, including American Citizen Services and visa appointments, during the strike.
U.S. citizens with appointments at the Embassy should plan for additional travel time and consider alternative transportation options.

U.S. citizens could expect:
• Significant disruptions to public transportation nationwide
• Protest activity associated with the strike
• Heavy police presence near demonstration areas
• Additional traffic congestion, including in the vicinity of the U.S. Embassy

Actions to Take:
• Avoid areas affected by protests and large gatherings
• Monitor local media for updates on traffic conditions and protest locations
• Allow extra time for travel and plan alternative transportation arrangements
• Keep a low profile and remain aware of your surroundings
• Review your personal security plans
• Ensure travel documents are up to date and easily accessible
• Enroll in the https://t.co/q8w0nZfWZo to receive security updates
• Follow local government authorities on social media for real-time information

For further information and assistance:
• Enroll in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program  (https://t.co/q8w0nZfWZo) to receive Alerts and make it easier to locate you in an emergency.
• Contact the U.S. Embassy in Manila, Philippines, located at 1201 Roxas Boulevard, at +(63) (2) 5301-2000, from 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday through Friday. After-hours emergency number for U.S. citizens is +(63) (2) 5301-2000.
• Call 1-888-407-4747 toll-free in the United States and Canada or 1-202-501-4444 from other countries from 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. Eastern Standard Time, Monday through Friday (except U.S. federal holidays).
• See the State Department’s travel website (https://t.co/Tiyt8sq7F9) for the Worldwide Caution, Travel Advisories, Alerts, and the Philippines Country Specific Information (https://t.co/ApMa3LxNZy).

NINJA TRADER - MORNING MARKET BRIEF
Wednesday, March 25, 2026

KEY THEMES
Markets are navigating a fragile equilibrium where Iran war headlines dictate direction, but technical positioning and month-end flows may force a short-term bounce despite deteriorating fundamentals. The dealer gamma profile-short downside, long upside-combined with $14 billion in pension rebalancing flows (97th percentile) into equities through quarter-end creates mechanical buying pressure that could catalyze a relief rally, particularly if Trump's reported 15-point Iran peace plan gains traction and oil pulls back further from triple-digit Brent. However, any rally faces structural headwinds: rates markets have repriced from cuts to net hikes through 2027, mortgage rates just hit 6.43% crushing housing demand into spring, and CTAs remain in sell programs with the S&P trading below all key moving averages. The real risk is that this becomes a bear market rally trap-pension flows provide temporary lift, but without genuine de-escalation in the Strait of Hormuz (jet fuel hoarding across Asia signals tightening supply chains), inflation concerns will keep the Fed hawkish and force another leg lower once rebalancing completes.

MARKET SNAPSHOT
Treasuries held Tuesday's gains with yields 3-4bp richer across the curve as oil weakness and peace plan hopes supported fixed income; focus shifts to today's $70bn 5-year auction after Tuesday's weak 2-year sale tailed by 1.8bp, with the 5-year WI at ~3.972% sitting 36bp cheaper than February's stop.

Risk assets found relief on reports of a US-drafted 15-point Iran peace plan, driving S&P futures +0.9%, Brent crude -6% below $99, and 2-year Treasury yields down 4bp to 3.86%, though investor caution remains elevated given Iran's continued attacks and reluctance to negotiate.

MACRO
ECB President Lagarde signaled readiness for decisive action if energy cost surges broaden into persistent inflation, emphasizing the bank's unconditional commitment to 2% inflation and willingness to adjust policy at any meeting once sufficient data on the shock's magnitude and duration is available.

Mortgage rates surged 13bp to 6.43% (highest since October) in their third consecutive weekly climb, causing purchase applications to drop 5.4% and refi applications to plunge 14.6%-a direct transmission of Treasury volatility into housing that threatens the critical spring selling season.

Treasury futures positioning unwinds that peaked March 2nd are near completion, with subsequent positioning shifts signaling new short bets targeting higher yields-an inflection point that will determine whether the recent bond selloff reverses or extends over coming weeks.

Fed rate cut expectations collapsed to year-lows with markets now pricing net hikes through April 2027 and first cut pushed to October 2027-a dramatic hawkish repricing that reflects stubbornly high inflation concerns and leaves 2026 pricing at net hikes versus the FOMC's projected cuts.

CORPORATE
ARM's launch of its first AI data center CPU delivering 2x performance per rack versus x86 with Meta as lead co-development partner and backing from OpenAI, Cloudflare, and Cerebras positions the company to capture $15bn in annual chip sales within five years-a significant diversification beyond its licensing model that validates its AI infrastructure strategy.

Peace plan hopes drove sector rotation with travel stocks (UAL +2.6%) and Mag 7 (AMZN +1.6%, TSLA +1.7%) rallying while energy and chemicals sold off; ARM surged 13% on its first proprietary chip launch targeting $15bn annual sales, and satellite stocks jumped on SpaceX IPO filing reports.

COMMODITY
Asian jet fuel hoarding intensifies as South Korea considers redirecting exports domestically, Philippines contemplates rationing, and Vietnam cuts flights-early signs of supply chain stress that could pressure airline margins and exacerbate inflation if Hormuz closure persists.

FLOWS AND POSITIONING
April positioning dynamics favor capital repatriation into US equities, technology, and quality as YTD ETF inflows of $518bn (30% ahead of last year, 5x historical average) amplify price impact in thin liquidity conditions where S&P 500 top-of-book depth sits at just $2.5M (3rd percentile vs. 2-year range).

Month-end and quarter-end rebalancing flows show US pensions estimated to buy $14 billion in equities (97th percentile vs. 3-year history) while selling equivalent bonds-a significant technical tailwind that could support equities into period-end despite macro headwinds.
